text:
SHENZHEN, China — A breakthrough in negotiations on services and investment under the Korea-China free trade agreement (FTA) lays the institutional groundwork for deeper economic cooperation between the two countries, presidential chief of staff for policy Ha Joon-kyung said.
The two countries announced they had reached a substantive agreement during a summit between President Lee Jae Myung and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Wednesday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China.
The breakthrough came eight years and eight months after negotiations began.
Speaking at a briefing, Ha said China accounts for a smaller share of Korea’s trade in services than of its trade in goods, leaving considerable room for growth.
As economic ties deepen, he said, companies begin investing in each other’s markets and providing services such as legal advice and cultural content under local laws and regulations.
Under the agreement, the two countries will improve access to each other’s markets in sectors including cultural content, tourism and legal services.
“Accordingly, the deal lays the institutional groundwork for a significant step forward in economic cooperation between the two countries,” Ha said.
The two countries also agreed to strengthen investment protections and make regulations more transparent.
The deal introduces a most-favored-nation obligation, requiring each country to treat companies from the other at least as favorably as it treats companies from third countries.
Ha also credited the Lee administration’s efforts to restore bilateral ties, saying reciprocal state visits helped improve relations and led Beijing to take a more flexible stance in the negotiations.
